title.value: An Empirical Study of Data Access Self-Admitted Technical Debt
title.justification: The title provides an accurate summary of the paper's focus on self-admitted technical debt specific to data access in software systems.
title.quote: An Empirical Study of Data Access Self-Admitted Technical Debt

extractions.description: This paper conducts an empirical study on self-admitted technical debt in data-intensive systems, focusing on data-access classes. It analyzes the prevalence, composition, and evolution of self-admitted technical debt across several open-source systems using relational and NoSQL databases.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on software engineering concepts related to technical debt and does not address Climate Change directly.
climate_change_is_central.quote:
Developers sometimes choose design and implementation shortcuts due to the pressure
from tight release schedules. However, shortcuts introduce technical debt that increases as the
software evolves.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address Climate Change, climate science, or sustainability at all. It is entirely focused on technical debt in software systems, specifically data-intensive systems.
primary_category.quote: In particular, we still do not know much about the prevalence and persistence of technical debt in data-intensive systems.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper lacks any references or discussions that directly link to Climate Change issues or categories.
secondary_categories.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this study has not been conducted before, and our findings fill a crucial gap in the literature of software engineering.

primary_sub_category.justification: Given the primary focus on software engineering concepts unrelated to Climate Change, there isn't an applicable sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: The rest of the paper is organized as follows...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The absence of climate-related content or analysis means no sub-categories apply.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Understanding the composition and distribution of the SATDs across software systems and their evolution could provide insights into managing technical debt efficiently.

applications.justification: No specific Climate Change applications are discussed in the study, as its focus is on software engineering and development practices.
applications.quote: We identified 15 new SATD categories, out of which 11 are specific to database access opera‐tions.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper primarily falls under software engineering research as it explores technical debt in software systems.
new_primary_category.quote: We present a large-scale empirical study on the prevalence, composition, and evolution of SATD in data-intensive systems.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The study specifically examines self-admitted technical debt management in data-intensive environments.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We conducted a manual analysis on representative data‐access SATDs to categorize them under the type of SATD refereed.
